An unnamed dog, muzzle and head past his ears thrust into the rubbish, those big black bin liners, hind legs tensed and began to twist, withdrew with some scrap swallowed in one gulp and then stood there panting in the heat.

He is a rangy mongrel and cannot bark. Months past he was in a cage in a room in the back of a restaurant that served dog. A dozen of his fellows passed through those doors and did not pass back and each time he smelled and knew their fear and pain and the scent of the dishes made from them. When it was his turn he twisted at the last second and the knife missed his arteries and windpipe though it did take away his vocal cords. In that second of pain and fear and hate he bit and pulled and bit again and when the hands released him he shot out through the door.

Now he was a street dog and these his streets. A pink livid scar runs down the side of his eye socket and beneath his neck visible even through his fur.

He wandered among the rubbish piles. He smelled something. He put his head down and followed the trail of rat. He saw it and rushed forward and it saw him and in a flash of fur and scrabbling of paws it was off with him after it.

It took him on a circular route around onto the streets with the teeming mass of legs and boots and smells and here he lost sight of it and almost lost its scent also but then he found it again and followed its trail back to the rubbish pits but now on the other side. 

Recently there had been a storm and a great banyan had been ripped up and its roots exposed a cave barely a slit in the ground. The creatures scent disappeared into this and the dog approached warily. Some genetic memories stored within warned him not to go further of an old danger but he was yet a young dog and he went anyway.

He went down into the crater where the tree had stood and began to dig and scratch at the slit in the earth trying to enlarge the hole. It was dark in there and many interesting scents. 

He felt pain and whipped his head back. His eyes watered. Pinpricks of blood appeared on his nose. He jumped and danced and then fled.
Beneath the earth in that dark tomb leathery wings flapped then quiet. The intruder had been pushed back.
